newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Hiveld sees Columbus losses shrinking.
newsitem.headline: Hiveld sees Columbus losses shrinking.

text.p: South Africa's Highveld Steel and Vanadium Ltd (Hiveld) said on Monday that losses at its joint venture unit Columbus Stainless were narrowing and that Hiveld would show a real increase in full year earnings.

"Columbus's operations have improved and its markets are capable of absorbing the additional materials as production levels increase gradually towards full capacity," managing director Trevor Jones said.
"While we were forecasting a modest improvement in earnings we are now forecasting a real improvement over 1996. Clearly we are now feeling a lot more confident," he told a media presentation.
Hiveld earlier announced half-year earnings per share up 42.2 cents from 41.5 cents in the previous half-year on attributable income which rose to 40.70 million rand from 39.30 million rand before.
Columbus's chief executive officer Fred Boshoff said results showed a loss before capitalisation of 203 million rand in the six month period compared with 319 million in the same period last year.
Mill yield per 100 kg of slab had improved reaching 74.0 percent in the first half of 1997, from 70.9 percent in the six months to December 1996 and 67.5 percent in the first half of 1996.
Boshoff said in July alone it had increased to 78 percent and that the target was 86 percent.
Capital expenditure for the group had also narrowed to almost 54.0 million rand from 149.7 million in the first half of 1996 and 253.9 million in the first half of 1993.
The production of vanadium slag had increased to 8.2 tonnes in the first half of this year from 7.7 tonnes in the first half of 1996.
Hiveld chairman Leslie Boyd said it was forecast that world vanadium consumption, in line with the high level of steel production, could reach record levels this year.
Boyd said ferrosilicon and medium carbon managanese were not likely to contribute significantly to Hiveld's earnings but that steel and vanadium would do well.
